After seeing the revised cases, I have withdrawn my rejection. 
Good work.
I made the test in IDE. All works fine. Please do what 5DN1L writes so that everyone kann approve.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: All works fine in IDE
@gr1sh, please follow up and modify the cases. Thanks.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Perfect marriage between very cool problem and very easy problem.
Why "angle is always a multiple of 90" ? I don't understand. Maybe, angle is any?

Goal
* Please remove the final paragraph.

Input
* Please add "space-separated" after "three".

* Please add the descriptions of x, y and a.

Constraints
* Please change both occurrences of -10^9 to -100.

* Please change both occurrences of 10^9 to 100.

* Please change "0 ≤ [[a]]" to "0 < [[a]]".

Cases
* These cases are the same:
  • Test 1
  • Validator 1
  Please revise Validator 1 so that its x and y differ from Test 1.

* Please add 4 more pairs of cases, one pair for each angle: 90, 180, 270 and 360. Two pairs should expect positive coordinates only, and the other two pairs should expect negative coordinates only.

* Please add 4 more pairs of cases, one pair for each angle: 90, 180, 270 and 360. In the input, x = 0 and y ≠ 0 for two pairs, and x ≠ 0 and y = 0 for the other two pairs.

* Please add a pair of cases where x = y = 0 in the input.

Thanks.

Hey g1rsh, I like this idea a lot!
A couple quick comments:
- Are you sure this can be played in reverse? I don't think that it's easy to understand without directions.

- 10^9 ≤ x ≤ 10^9 and 10^9 ≤ y ≤ 10^9 means that x and y are always one value...

- You wrote `[]y']]` in your output- did you mean [y']?
Thank you for your feedback. I have already made the changes you mentioned

Thank you for making the changes. However, the newly added Tests/Validators 5 to 7 are mixing different scenarios within each pair. Please remove those cases and add 8 new tests and 8 new validators as follows. Of course, you can recycle the removed cases as part of the new 8 pairs.

* Please add 4 more pairs of cases, one pair for each angle: 90, 180, 270 and 360. Two pairs should expect positive coordinates only, and the other two pairs should expect negative coordinates only.

* Please add 4 more pairs of cases, one pair for each angle: 90, 180, 270 and 360. In the input, x = 0 and y ≠ 0 for two pairs, and x ≠ 0 and y = 0 for the other two pairs.

Thanks again.
Because if it wasn't, you'd have to use cos and sin, which would complicate the problem but would be even more interesting
All comments have been taken into account, and the statement and tests have been updated accordingly.
All comments have been taken into account, and the statement and tests have been updated accordingly.
Thanks. The revised cases are fine now.

Nice- one more thing I forgot to mention- make sure that you make all of the values you compare x, y, and a to in the Constraints section {Constants}.

Otherwise, I love it!

I would say this is definitely playable in Reverse. The angle is always a multiple of 90, which makes it relatively easy to understand it's an angle. The similarity between the first two numbers in input and the two numbers in output also make it clear that the first two numbers are "data" to be transformed and the third number is the "operation" to be applied on them. And the operation is pretty clear in the first test case: for 90, replace (x,y) with (-y,x)
